media.caption: This is a modern photograph of a restored mound. NPS explains that the visible walls and mounds at Mound City were reconstructed using surviving bases, documents and field research. A present-day view therefore contains both ancient evidence and modern interpretation.

media.caption: A survey is evidence of what observers recorded, using their methods and assumptions. It is not a photograph of the ancient gathering place. The name Hopewell came from a later landowner, not a surviving name for all its builders. This institutional reproduction has limited resolution.

media.caption: Squier and Davis surveyed Mound City in 1846 and published the plan in 1848 as Plate XIX. The enclosure and mound symbols appear beside the Scioto River; a canal and other recorded features share the sheet. This is a later survey, not a single ancient construction phase. It is a different plan from the existing North Fork Works image of Hopewell Mound Group. The small source reproduction retains its original limits.
